findings.title: `shared-packages.ts` is an unused cross-package probe wrapper
findings.why_it_matters: Dead code is a maintenance liability: future developers assume it has a consumer and hesitate to delete. It also duplicates the shared package API surface, so changes to `@crm/auth` or `@crm/config` may appear to need mirroring here even though nothing uses the wrappers.
findings.evidence: `rg -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx' "shared-packages" apps/mobile` returned no imports. The file only re-exports `parseEnv`, `createCrmAuthClient`, and their types, but the real providers import directly from `@crm/config` and `@crm/auth`.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete `apps/mobile/src/lib/shared-packages.ts`. If U2 needs a probe that cross-package imports typecheck, keep it as a one-off test or type-test file outside `src/` (e.g., under a `typecheck-probes/` folder), not in the shipped source tree.

findings.title: `MutationButton` is exported but never used
findings.why_it_matters: An unused component adds bundle weight and sets a false expectation that forms use it. New Activity currently hand-rolls its own loading/success state, so the abstraction is either premature or orphaned.
findings.evidence: `rg -g '*.ts' -g '*.tsx' "MutationButton" apps/mobile` only matches the definition file. `NewActivityScreen` uses the raw `Button` primitive and its own `justSaved`/`submitting` state instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) delete the component and reintroduce it when at least two forms need it, or (b) migrate `NewActivityScreen` to use `MutationButton` so the abstraction earns its keep.

findings.title: Empty `useConvexNetworkListener` hook is dead code
findings.why_it_matters: A no-op hook wrapped in a named abstraction adds indirection without behavior. The 'future seam' comment will rot; the next developer has to read it to discover it does nothing.
findings.evidence: The hook's only effect has an empty body with a comment: `// Future: force a token re-check...`. It reads `isOnline` from context but performs no action.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `useConvexNetworkListener` and the call site in `ConvexClientProvider`. Re-add a real listener when there is concrete logic (e.g., forcing a Convex reconnect).

findings.title: Mobile stubs `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` to satisfy shared env schema
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile is coupled to a server-only secret it does not need. A future change to validation rules or a mistaken `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix on the stub could leak a secret or break startup. The abstraction in `@crm/config` is not truly platform-agnostic if mobile has to fake a field.
findings.evidence: `mobileEnv()` passes `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_STUB ?? 'mobile-client-not-server'` to `parseEnv` solely because the shared schema marks it required.
findings.suggested_fix: Split `@crm/config` into a client-safe schema (CONVEX_URL, CONVEX_SITE_URL, SITE_URL, NODE_ENV) and a server/full schema that adds `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. Mobile should validate and consume only the client schema.

findings.title: Mobile auth client duplicates shared factory plugin configuration
findings.why_it_matters: Two parallel plugin lists (one in `@crm/auth/src/auth-client.ts`, one here) mean a security or behavior change must be remembered in both places. Over time they will drift, producing subtle differences between web and mobile auth behavior.
findings.evidence: `auth-client.ts` calls `createAuthClient` from `better-auth/react` and manually lists `inferAdditionalFields()`, `crossDomainClient(...)`, and `convexClient()`. The same plugin set is hard-coded inside `createCrmAuthClient` in `@crm/auth`, but mobile cannot reuse it because that factory uses the non-React `better-auth/client` entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor `@crm/auth` to expose a React-aware client builder (e.g., `createCrmAuthClient({ react: true, ... })` or a separate `createCrmReactAuthClient`) that reuses the same plugin assembly logic. Mobile then imports that builder instead of hand-rolling the plugins.

findings.title: `format-date.ts` is a verbatim copy of the web utility
findings.why_it_matters: Two copies of the same formatter will drift. A bug fix, locale change, or new pattern applied to one copy is likely to be forgotten in the other, breaking the stated goal of keeping web and mobile date strings identical.
findings.evidence: The file header explicitly states it was 'Copied verbatim from `apps/web/src/lib/format-date.ts` (DO NOT modify the web file). Kept in sync so mobile and web render identical date strings.' Manual sync is a classic anti-pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the Intl-based formatter to a shared package (e.g., `@crm/shared/date-format` or `@crm/format`) and consume it from both `apps/web` and `apps/mobile`. If a platform-specific divergence is ever required, branch inside the shared module with a clear comment rather than forking the file.

findings.title: `NewActivity` hand-rolls Zod schemas from domain const arrays
findings.why_it_matters: The screen is coupled to the exact shape of `ACTIVITY_TYPES` and `ENTITY_TYPES` and has to cast them into Zod enum shapes. Adding a new type requires edits in both `@crm/domain` and this screen, and the casts suppress useful type errors.
findings.evidence: `const USER_ACTIVITY_TYPES = ACTIVITY_TYPES.filter(...)` is redefined locally, then cast with `as unknown as [string, ...string[]]` for `z.enum`. The same filtering logic also appears in `activity-type-picker.tsx`.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `@crm/domain` export Zod schemas for `ActivityType` and `EntityType` (and a `UserActivityType` subset), then import and use them directly. This removes the casts and centralizes the 'status_change is system-only' rule.

findings.title: Invoice detail reimplements overdue classification already in `invoice-row.tsx`
findings.why_it_matters: The overdue rule is duplicated between the list row and the detail screen. A future change—such as a grace period or a different 'posted' state handling—must be made in both places or the UI will disagree with itself.
findings.evidence: `[id].tsx` computes `overdue` inline with `state === 'posted' && amountDue > 0 && typeof dueDate === 'number' && dueDate < now`. `invoice-row.tsx` exports the same logic as `isInvoiceOverdue(inv, now)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `isInvoiceOverdue` and a shared `formatInvoiceStatus`/badge helper to a dedicated invoice utility module (e.g., `@/lib/invoices.ts`) and import it in both `invoice-row.tsx` and `[id].tsx`.

findings.title: Avatar initials logic is duplicated between More and Settings
findings.why_it_matters: The same name-to-initials transformation is implemented twice with slightly different wrappers (inline vs `useMemo`). Future tweaks to multi-name handling or fallback behavior will diverge, producing inconsistent avatars.
findings.evidence: `more.tsx` lines 56-61 and `settings.tsx` lines 55-62 both compute `displayName` and `initials` by splitting on whitespace and upper-casing the first characters.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `getInitials(name?: string | null, fallback?: string): string` to `@/lib/user-display.ts` (or similar) and consume it from both screens.

findings.title: `toAuthSession` duplicates session validation from `@crm/auth/session.ts`
findings.why_it_matters: Two slightly different guards for the same Better Auth payload create confusion about which is authoritative. If the required fields change, one location may accept data the other rejects, leading to silent auth bugs.
findings.evidence: `auth-provider.tsx` defines `toAuthSession` checking `s.id`, `u.id`, and `u.email`. `@crm/auth/src/session.ts` already exports `isSessionPayload` and `toSessionUser` for the same purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `isSessionPayload` and `toSessionUser` from `@crm/auth` inside the provider. Keep the provider focused on dispatching machine events rather than redefining session shape validation.

findings.title: `EmptyState` bypasses the project's `Text` primitive
findings.why_it_matters: A design-system component that imports raw `Text` from `react-native` undermines the typography primitive the team created. Future typography changes must be hunted across both primitive and ad-hoc raw text usages.
findings.evidence: `empty-state.tsx` imports `Text` from `react-native` and applies manual Tailwind classes, while every other screen uses `@/components/ui/text` with typed variants.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the raw `Text` imports with `import { Text } from '@/components/ui/text'` and use `variant` props to express the title/body/caption hierarchy.

residual_risks: `babel.nativewind.js` is a local fork of the upstream NativeWind babel preset. It solves the Reanimated 3/4 mismatch today, but every NativeWind upgrade now requires manually reconciling this file against upstream changes.

`metro.config.js` maintains a regex-based browser-only blocklist. Adding a new web-only shared dependency requires updating both the blocklist and the corresponding shared-package import discipline; there is no automated guard that a new web-only dep has been caught.

`mocks/react-slot.tsx` exists solely to satisfy a vestigial `expo-router` require. If Expo Router removes that require in a future release, the stub and Metro alias become unnecessary indirection that nobody will dare delete.
testing_gaps: No automated dead-code/unused-export check (e.g., `knip`) for the mobile app. A tool would have caught `shared-packages.ts`, `MutationButton`, and `useConvexNetworkListener` automatically.

No test that verifies `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (or any server-only secret) never reaches the mobile bundle. A bundle analysis / forbidden-import test would reduce the risk introduced by the current env-schema coupling.
No test enforcing parity between `apps/web/src/lib/format-date.ts` and `apps/mobile/src/lib/format-date.ts`. The current 'copied verbatim' convention is not verified.

Auth provider integration tests are missing: there is good unit coverage of the reducer, but no test that `AuthProvider` + `authClient` correctly dispatches `SESSION_RESOLVED`, `SIGN_IN_FAILURE`, and `TOKEN_REVOKED` in sequence.
